mainTopic: Wool shed by a blemished בכור: the dispute of עקביא and the חכמים, ריש לקיש's condition of a מומחה's permission, and the two versions of רבי יוחנן on the ברייתא of mixed-up blemished animals
overview: A blemished בכור may be slaughtered and eaten, but its wool may not be used while it is alive. So what about wool that fell off by itself before the animal was slaughtered or died? The משנה gives two versions of the dispute between עקביא בן מהללאל and the חכמים. In רבי יהודה's version they argue about an animal that was later slaughtered. In רבי יוסי's version they argue about an animal that later died. The גמרא explains that, for רבי יוסי, everyone permits the wool in the slaughtered case. ריש לקיש adds that the argument is only where a מומחה had already permitted the animal: the חכמים forbid the wool so the owner will not delay the slaughter. רב ששת challenges ריש לקיש from a ברייתא about mixed-up blemished animals, and רבא defends him. In ארץ ישראל, רבי ירמיה rejects this whole Babylonian reading. He brings two versions of רבי יוחנן, each tied to a different dispute about lost טומאה, and the גמרא explains why each אמורא rejected the other's version. The amud ends with a new challenge to ריש לקיש from a ברייתא about wool plucked from an unblemished בכור, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רבי יהודה's version of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its first version of the case. Here the חכמים forbid the wool, and this version is said in the name of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and the חכמים forbid it. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a sentence that began earlier. The case was: hair fell off a blemished בכור, someone put it in a window, and later the animal was slaughtered. עקביא בן מהללאל permits that hair, the חכמים forbid it, and this whole version comes from רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's version, the argument is about an animal that was later slaughtered. Normally, once a blemished בכור is slaughtered, its wool is permitted. The question is whether hair that fell off while the animal was still alive is also permitted. The חכמים say no, because that hair came off at a time when the wool was still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: These are the words of רבי יהודה; it tells us who reported this version

phrases.english: and the Sages forbid it,
phrases.notes: Continues the case earlier: the hair fell off, was put in a window, and afterward the animal was slaughtered.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the argument is about hair that fell off and the animal was later slaughtered. עקביא permits it and the חכמים forbid it.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's version: the dispute is about an animal that died
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees about where the argument is. He says עקביא only permitted the hair in a case where the animal later died, not where it was slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to him: עקביא בן מהללאל did not permit in that case. Rather, the case is hair of a blemished animal that fell off, and he put it in a window, and afterward the animal died. In that case עקביא בן מהללאל permits and the חכמים forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי tells רבי יהודה that he has the case wrong. In רבי יוסי's version, the argument is about hair that fell off when the animal later died instead of being slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור that dies without שחיטה must be buried, and everything attached to it is forbidden. רבי יוסי says this is the case where עקביא still permits the hair that fell off earlier, while the חכמים forbid it. So the two תנאים disagree only about which case the argument is in. The wording 'not in this case' will cause a question in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not permit in this case
A window or wall niche, used to store something

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בָּזֶה הִתִּיר עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל,
phrases.english: Akavya ben Mahalalel did not permit in this case,
phrases.notes: 'This case' means the slaughtered case from רבי יהודה's version.

phrases.english: rather, hair of a blemished animal that fell off
and he put it in a window, and afterward the animal died —
in this case Akavya ben Mahalalel permits
and the Sages forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: לֹא בָּזֶה הִתִּיר עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the dispute, moving it from the slaughtered case to the dead-animal case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, the argument is about hair that fell off and the animal later died. עקביא permits it and the חכמים forbid it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא's question in step 4 is aimed at the words 'not in this case.'

steps.title: Wool hanging loosely from a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules on wool that is half detached and dangling from the בכור. If it looks like part of the fleece, it is permitted. If it does not, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wool that is dangling from a firstborn: what looks like part of the fleece is permitted, and what does not look like part of the fleece is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a new, related case: wool that has not fully fallen off but is hanging loose. It sorts the wool by whether it still looks like part of the animal's fleece.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the loose wool still looks like part of the fleece, it is treated like the rest of the wool, which is permitted after שחיטה. If it no longer looks like part of the fleece, it is treated like wool that fell off while the animal was alive, which is forbidden. So appearance decides which category the wool belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: Wool that hangs loose and is partly detached
Fleece, or the shearing of it

phrases.english: wool that is dangling from a firstborn,
what looks like part of the fleece is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ נִרְאֶה עִם הַגִּיזָּה — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: and what does not look like part of the fleece is forbidden.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dangling wool that looks like part of the fleece is permitted along with the fleece. Dangling wool that does not look like part of the fleece is forbidden.

steps.title: Why would עקביא forbid the slaughtered case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבי יוסי's wording seems to say עקביא forbids the wool when the animal was slaughtered. That is illogical: if he permits it when the animal died, he should surely permit it when it was slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This implies that he forbids it when the animal was slaughtered. But now that he permits it when the animal died, is it even necessary to say he permits it when it was slaughtered?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by questioning רבי יוסי's words 'not in this case.' Those words seem to mean that עקביא forbids the wool in the slaughtered case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead בכור is the stricter case, because even its attached wool is forbidden and must be buried. A slaughtered בכור is the easier case, because its attached wool is permitted. So if עקביא permits the fallen hair in the strict case, he must also permit it in the easy case. It cannot be that he forbids it there.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that…; it opens a 'surely' (קל וחומר) argument
Is it even necessary to say?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is asking about the חכמים. The question is only about what רבי יוסי's wording implies about עקביא's view of the slaughtered case.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא's discussion.

phrases.english: This implies that he (Akavya) forbids it when the animal was slaughtered,
now that he permits it when the animal died,
is it even necessary to say he permits it when it was slaughtered?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּאָסַר, הַשְׁתָּא בְּמֵת — שָׁרֵי, שְׁחָטוֹ מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's wording 'לֹא בָּזֶה הִתִּיר עֲקַבְיָא'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording implies that עקביא forbids the slaughtered case. But a קל וחומר from the stricter dead-animal case shows he must permit it.

steps.title: In the slaughtered case everyone permits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוסי did not mean עקביא forbids the slaughtered case. He meant that this is not where the argument is, because in the slaughtered case everyone permits the wool. The argument is only about a dead animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he meant: it is not in this case that עקביא permits and the חכמים forbid. When the animal was slaughtered, everyone agrees it is permitted. Where they argue is when it died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by reading רבי יוסי's words differently. 'Not in this case' means 'this is not where they argue.' It does not mean that עקביא forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the slaughtered case, even the חכמים agree the fallen hair is permitted, so there is no argument there at all. The only argument is in the dead-animal case: עקביא permits and the חכמים forbid. This removes the illogical implication from step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; it introduces a new reading

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי as the גמרא explains him: if the animal was slaughtered, everyone permits the hair that fell off earlier. If the animal died, עקביא permits it and the חכמים forbid it.

phrases.english: Rather, it is not in this case that Akavya permits
and the Sages forbid,
when he slaughtered it, everyone agrees it is permitted,
where they argue is when it died.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לֹא בָּזֶה הִתִּיר עֲקַבְיָא וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִין
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not in this case' seemed to mean that עקביא forbids the slaughtered case.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Not in this case' means there is no argument there, because everyone permits the slaughtered case. The argument is only about a dead animal.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: The Argument Is Only When an Expert Permitted the Animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי quotes ריש לקיש. The argument between עקביא and the חכמים is only where a מומחה had already permitted the blemished בכור. The חכמים forbid the wool so the owner will not delay slaughtering. עקביא does not make that גזירה. Without a מומחה's permission, everyone forbids the wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of ריש לקיש: The argument is in a case where an expert permitted the animal. One side holds we make a decree, in case the owner comes to delay slaughtering it. The other side holds we do not make that decree. But if an expert did not permit it, everyone agrees the wool is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש tells us exactly which case the argument in the משנה is about. It is the case where a מומחה already declared the בכור's blemish a real one, which permits slaughtering it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a מומחה permits the animal, the owner may slaughter it right away. The חכמים worry that if he may use the wool it sheds, he will keep the animal alive longer to collect more wool. So they forbid the wool. עקביא does not worry about this. If no מומחה permitted the animal, the wool is still fully holy, so nobody permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: An expert permitted it (declared the blemish a real one, so the animal may be slaughtered)
We make a rabbinic decree (a protective rule)
To delay it (to keep the animal alive longer)

steps.whyThisMatters: This defines the whole argument. It is not about the basic holiness of the wool. It is about a protective rabbinic decree.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the חכמים forbid the wool because it is truly holy. In the case where a מומחה permitted the animal, their reason is only a גזירה against delaying the slaughter.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said that Reish Lakish said:
The dispute is where an expert permitted it,
phrases.notes: An expert confirmed the blemish, so the בכור may be slaughtered.

phrases.english: for one master holds: we decree
phrases.notes: This is the חכמים.

phrases.english: lest he come to delay it (its slaughter),
and the other master holds: we do not decree,
phrases.notes: This is עקביא בן מהללאל.

phrases.english: but if an expert did not permit it —
all agree it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּשֶׁהִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where the dispute is (died vs. slaughtered) to what condition it needs (a מומחה's permission) and what the reason behind it is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is only where a מומחה permitted the animal. The חכמים forbid the wool through a גזירה against delaying slaughter, and עקביא does not make that גזירה. Without a מומחה's permission, everyone forbids the wool.

steps.title: רב ששת Quotes a ברייתא About Mixed-Up Blemished Animals
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת begins a challenge to ריש לקיש. He quotes a ברייתא: blemished animals forbid a mixture no matter how small their share, while רבי יוסי says 'יבקר', investigate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת raised an objection: Blemished animals forbid a mixture in any amount. And רבי יוסי says: Let it be investigated.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת is setting up a challenge. Here he only quotes the source text. The argument against ריש לקיש is built in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא records an argument between a תנא קמא, who forbids everything, and רבי יוסי, who says to investigate. What this argument is really about is not yet clear. The גמרא must first explain it, and only then will the challenge to ריש לקיש become clear.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection (usually from a ברייתא or משנה)
They forbid in any amount (they are never cancelled out by the majority)
Let it be investigated or checked

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raised an objection:
Blemished ones forbid (a mixture) in any amount,
and Rabbi Yosei says: Let it be investigated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge against ריש לקיש's statement in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that the dispute about a בכור's wool is only where a מומחה permitted the animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the ברייתא is explained as being about wool of a blemished בכור (step 9), רבי יוסי's 'יבקר' will be read as checking whether the blemish is permanent or temporary (step 10). That would permit the wool even though no מומחה permitted the animal, which contradicts ריש לקיש.

steps.title: What Does 'Investigate' Mean?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת recalls an earlier discussion of the ברייתא. If 'יבקר' means find the blemished animal and remove it, that would mean the תנא קמא forbids the rest even after removal. That makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: What does 'investigate' mean? If you say it means he should find the blemished one and take it out, then by implication the first תנא says no, you may not do that?
steps.whatsHappening: Before using the ברייתא as a challenge, the גמרא asks what רבי יוסי's word 'יבקר' means. It then rejects the most obvious reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple reading is that you should look for the blemished animal and remove it. But then the תנא קמא would be saying the rest stay forbidden even after the blemished one is gone. No one would say that. So the ברייתא must be about a different kind of case.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (the גמרא recalls an earlier discussion)
If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
What does 'investigate' mean?
If you say: (find) the one that is blemished, and remove it —
then by implication the first tanna says no (that this does not help)?
phrases.notes: This is rhetorical. It is impossible that the תנא קמא would forbid the rest after removal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the ברייתא quoted in step 7 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יוסי means by 'יבקר', given that the simple reading makes the תנא קמא's view illogical.

steps.title: רב נחמן: The ברייתא Is About a Firstborn's Wool Mixed With Ordinary Wool
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, explains the ברייתא's case. It is about shearings of a blemished בכור that got mixed with ordinary wool. The תנא קמא is רבי יהודה, who says the חכמים forbid the wool even when the animal was slaughtered. רבי יוסי follows his own view, that the חכמים permit it when slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: Here we are dealing with shearings of a blemished בכור that got mixed with ordinary wool. And who is the first תנא? It is רבי יהודה, who says: if they were slaughtered, the חכמים forbid. And רבי יוסי follows his own reasoning, for he says: if they were slaughtered, the חכמים permit.
steps.whatsHappening: This answers the question from step 8. The ברייתא is about wool, not live animals, and it links the two opinions to the two versions of the argument in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the case is wool of a בכור mixed into ordinary wool, the תנא קמא forbids the whole mixture. That matches רבי יהודה, for whom the חכמים forbid the wool even of a slaughtered בכור. רבי יוסי says to investigate, meaning check how the wool came about, because for him wool of a slaughtered בכור is permitted. רב ששת will use this explanation to challenge ריש לקיש, and that challenge continues next.

keyTerms.meaning: The shearings or wool of a firstborn animal
Following his own reasoning (consistent with his view elsewhere)

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the ברייתא directly to the two versions in our משנה (רבי יהודה in step 1, רבי יוסי in step 2). This is the base for רב ששת's challenge against ריש לקיש.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer is still part of רב ששת's quote of an earlier discussion. It is not the end of the sugya. רב ששת's actual challenge to ריש לקיש comes next.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא בְּגִיזַּת בְּכוֹר בַּעַל מוּם עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: Here we are dealing with the shearings of a blemished firstborn,
that became mixed with non-sacred shearings.
And who is the first tanna?
It is Rabbi Yehuda, who says:
if they were slaughtered, the Rabbis forbid (the wool).
phrases.notes: This matches step 1, רבי יהודה's version of the משנה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei follows his own reasoning, for he says:
if they were slaughtered, the Rabbis permit (the wool).
phrases.notes: This matches steps 2 and 5: in the slaughtered case, everyone permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ הָכָא בְּגִיזַּת בְּכוֹר בַּעַל מוּם עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 by placing the ברייתא in a new case and linking its opinions to the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is about wool of a blemished בכור mixed with ordinary wool. The תנא קמא is רבי יהודה (the חכמים forbid even a slaughtered בכור's wool). רבי יוסי follows his view that the חכמים permit a slaughtered בכור's wool, so one should investigate the wool's origin.

steps.title: רב ששת finishes his challenge from the word 'investigate'
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת argues that רבי יוסי's 'יבוקר' means checking whether the blemish is permanent. If so, the wool would be permitted even if no מומחה had permitted the animal. That contradicts ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the ברייתא teaches that רבי יוסי says 'let it be investigated.' What does 'investigated' mean? Doesn't it mean checking whether it is a permanent blemish or a temporary blemish, even though no expert had permitted it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת now finishes the attack he started in Step 7. He uses רבי יוסי's word 'יבוקר' to show that wool can be permitted without a מומחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to Step 9, the ברייתא is about wool from a blemished בכור that got mixed with other wool. If רבי יוסי says to check whether the blemish is permanent, then a permanent blemish is enough to permit the wool. No prior permission from a מומחה is needed. But ריש לקיש said that without a מומחה's permission, everyone forbids the wool.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be investigated or examined
A permanent blemish, which allows a בכור to be slaughtered
A temporary blemish, which does not allow it

phrases.english: And it teaches: 'Let it be investigated.'
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי's word in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: What does 'let it be investigated' mean?
Does it not mean: whether it is a permanent blemish
or whether it is a temporary blemish,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב שֶׁלֹּא הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה.
phrases.english: even though an expert did not permit it?
phrases.notes: This is the punchline against ריש לקיש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This uses the reading from Step 9 (the ברייתא is about wool, and רבי יוסי permits slaughtered wool) to complete רב ששת's challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim in Step 6 that without a מומחה's permission, everyone forbids the wool
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'יבוקר' seems to mean checking the type of blemish. That means a permanent blemish alone permits the wool, with no מומחה needed.

steps.title: רבא: 'investigate' means check whether an expert permitted it
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that 'יבוקר' means checking whether a מומחה had already permitted the animal. If so, the wool is permitted. If not, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: No. 'Let it be investigated' means: if an expert permitted it, yes, it is permitted. If not, it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends ריש לקיש. He gives the word 'יבוקר' a different meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא agrees that some checking is needed, but he changes what is being checked. The question is not what kind of blemish it was. The question is whether a מומחה had already given permission. This fits ריש לקיש exactly.

phrases.english: Rava said: No.
Let it be investigated: if an expert permitted it, yes, it is permitted.
And if not, it is not permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא; יְבוּקַּר, אִי הִתִּירוֹ מוּמְחֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's challenge in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the key word in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יבוקר' means check whether the blemish is permanent, so no מומחה is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'יבוקר' means check whether a מומחה already permitted the animal, which agrees with ריש לקיש.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה rejects the Babylonian discussion
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports this whole discussion in ארץ ישראל. רבי ירמיה sharply rejects it and calls the Babylonian explanations 'dark' teachings.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין went up to ארץ ישראל, he said this teaching before רבי ירמיה. רבי ירמיה said: Foolish Babylonians! Because they live in a dark land, they say dark, unclear teachings!
steps.whatsHappening: The scene moves to ארץ ישראל. רבי ירמיה rejects the way the Babylonians explained the ברייתא, and this sets up his own explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His rejection is aimed at the whole Babylonian approach that reads the ברייתא as being about wool from a בכור (Step 9 onward). He is not just quarreling with רבא's single answer. The reason for the rejection comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: When he went up to ארץ ישראל
Teachings that are dark or unclear

phrases.english: When Ravin went up to Eretz Yisrael,
he said this teaching before Rabbi Yirmeya.
He said: Foolish Babylonians!
Because they live in a dark land,
they say teachings that are dark!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סְלֵיק רָבִין, אַמְרַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the entire Babylonian line of explanation from Steps 9 through 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole Babylonian reading of the ברייתא as dealing with wool
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: They missed רבי יוחנן's explanation, which is given in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי ירמיה is not only rejecting רבא's last answer. He is rejecting the starting point of the whole Babylonian discussion, which is רב נחמן's claim that the ברייתא is about wool.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the dispute is where one searched and did not find
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes רבי יוחנן. The ברייתא is about the blemished animals themselves, and the argument is in a case where someone searched for the blemished animal and did not find it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't they hear what רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן? The argument is when he searched and did not find.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives the explanation the Babylonians missed. רבי יוחנן puts the argument in a completely different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוחנן's reading, the ברייתא is not about wool at all. It is about blemished animals mixed into a flock. If you find the blemished animal and take it out, everyone agrees the rest is permitted. That removes the difficulty from Step 8. The argument is only when you searched and could not find it.

keyTerms.meaning: He searched and did not find

phrases.english: Did they not hear this

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: which Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
The dispute is where he searched and did not find it.
phrases.notes: The case is about the animals themselves, not their wool.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לְהוּ הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבי ירמיה's rejection in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument in the ברייתא is about a case where one searched for the blemished animal and did not find it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the question from Step 8 in a new way. If the animal was found and removed, everyone permits the rest. So there is no need to move the case over to wool.

steps.title: The dispute matches רבי מאיר and the Rabbis on presumed impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ברייתא's argument follows the argument between רבי מאיר and the רבנן. רבי מאיר holds that anything with a known status of טומאה stays טמא until the טומאה is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they argue about the same point as רבי מאיר and the רבנן. As we learned: רבי מאיר used to say that anything that had a status of impurity stays in its impurity forever, until the impurity becomes known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the argument in the ברייתא to a well-known argument found elsewhere. It begins quoting that source, which is set up to continue next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you searched and did not find the problem, does the problem stay in place? רבי מאיר says yes: a known status stays until you actually find the cause. The תנא קמא, who forbids the flock, matches this view. רבי יוסי's opposing view will be matched to the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: An established status of ritual impurity

phrases.english: And they argue about the dispute of Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis,
as we learned in a mishnah, that Rabbi Meir would say:
phrases.notes: The source is פסחים י׳ע״א.

phrases.english: Anything that was in a presumed status of impurity
remains in its impurity forever,
until the impurity becomes known.
phrases.notes: For example, a field with a grave stays טמא until the grave itself is found.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָמִיפַּלְגִי בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבָּנַן, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's case by linking it to a known argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, an established status of טומאה stays until the source is actually found. Searching without finding it is not enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the argument in the ברייתא is part of a general question: does a search that fails to find the cause remove an established status?

steps.title: The Rabbis say: dig down to bedrock
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן finish the source from step 14. A person digs until he reaches bedrock or untouched soil. If he still finds nothing, the טומאה is treated as gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis say: he keeps digging until he reaches bedrock or virgin soil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the source it started in step 14 and gives the view of the חכמים, who argue with רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said known טומאה stays in place until it is found. The חכמים say a full search is enough: dig until you reach ground that was never disturbed, and if you find nothing, the טומאה is gone. Applied to our ברייתא, the first תנא follows רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי follows the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: virgin soil that was never dug or disturbed

steps.whatToRemember: In רבי חייא בר אבא's version of רבי יוחנן, the person searched and did NOT find the בעל מום. The first תנא is like רבי מאיר (it stays in place), and רבי יוסי is like the חכמים (a full search is enough).

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
He digs until he reaches
bedrock or virgin soil.
phrases.notes: No טומאה can lie below soil that was never disturbed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the רבי מאיר and רבנן source cited in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A full search down to undisturbed ground is enough. If nothing is found, the טומאה is treated as gone.

steps.title: A second version of רבי יוחנן: the animal was searched for and found
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי reports רבי יוחנן differently. The argument is in a case where the person searched and DID find a blemished animal. The argument matches the dispute between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the argument is in a case where he checked and found a blemished animal. They argue about the same thing that רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different report of what רבי יוחנן said about the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, nothing was found. Here, a blemished animal was found. The question is whether we can assume that the animal found is the same one that was lost.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a continuation of the earlier version. It is a competing report of רבי יוחנן's words, with a different case and a different parallel dispute.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
The dispute is when he examined and found
and they disagree in the dispute
of Rabbi and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a rival version of רבי יוחנן's explanation, replacing the 'searched and not found' case with 'searched and found'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא's argument is about a case where a blemished animal was found. It parallels the dispute between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: The source: a lost grave in a field
steps.stepSummary: A field with a lost grave makes anyone who enters it טמא. If a grave is later found, רבי says we assume it is the lost one, so entering the rest of the field leaves a person טהור. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the whole field must be checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: a field where a grave was lost, anyone who enters it is טמא. If a grave was found in it, anyone who enters is טהור, because I say the grave that was lost is the grave that was found. These are the words of רבי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: the whole field must be checked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that contains the dispute between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, which רבי אסי pointed to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי assumes that the item found is the item that was lost. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not rely on that assumption and requires a full search. Applied to our ברייתא, the first תנא is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and רבי יוסי is like רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'for I say': a reasoning formula that introduces an assumption

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that 'the one found is the one lost' is a well-known principle that comes up in many places in ש״ס.

phrases.english: As it is taught: a field in which a grave was lost,
one who enters it is impure.
If a grave was found in it,
one who enters it is pure,
for I say: the grave that was lost
is the grave that was found. These are the words of Rabbi.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
The entire field must be examined.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Cites the source of the dispute that רבי אסי referred to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי says the grave that was found is assumed to be the lost one. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל requires checking the whole field.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי אסי explain it like רבי חייא בר אבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אסי did not accept the other version, which explained the case as 'searched and not found'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אסי, what is his reason for not explaining it like רבי חייא בר אבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי אסי rejected the first version. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version, reported by רבי חייא בר אבא, compared our case to רבי מאיר and the רבנן about digging. The גמרא wants to know what bothered רבי אסי about that comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: he did not say it like...

phrases.english: And Rabbi Asi, what is the reason

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא?
phrases.english: that he did not say like Rabbi Chiya bar Abba?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אַסִּי, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two versions and asks why רבי אסי did not adopt the first.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What flaw did רבי אסי see in the 'searched and not found' explanation?

steps.title: טומאה can be carried off, but an animal can't vanish
steps.stepSummary: With טומאה, we can say a raven or mouse carried it away, so not finding it means it is gone. A blemished animal in a flock has nowhere to disappear to.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: it makes sense with טומאה, since we can say a raven came and took it, or a mouse came and took it. But here, where would the blemished animal go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי אסי: the comparison to lost טומאה does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים can say a full search proves the טומאה is gone, because small items really can be carried away. A whole animal cannot simply leave the flock. So 'searched and not found' does not make sense for our case, and רבי אסי explained the case as 'searched and found' instead.

phrases.english: He would say to you: granted, regarding impurity,
say a raven came and took it,
a mouse came and took it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָכָא — בַּעַל מוּם לְהֵיכָא אָזֵיל?
phrases.english: but here, where did the blemished animal go?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18 by pointing out a weakness in רבי חייא בר אבא's comparison.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lost טומאה could have been carried off by an animal, but a blemished animal cannot disappear from a flock. So the 'not found' case does not fit.

steps.title: How would the other אמורא respond?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי חייא בר אבא would deal with רבי אסי's point.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי חייא בר אבא and asks how he would answer. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי's point seems strong: a whole animal cannot just vanish. The גמרא wants to know how the first version can still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: and the other one (the other opinion)?

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: Refers to רבי חייא בר אבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי אסי's argument into a question for רבי חייא בר אבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does רבי חייא בר אבא explain the case of an animal that was searched for and not found?

steps.title: The blemish was temporary and healed
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא would say the animal didn't disappear. Its blemish was temporary and healed, so it can no longer be recognized.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it was a temporary blemish, and it healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי חייא בר אבא: the blemished animal is still in the flock, but it looks normal now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not found' does not mean the animal left. It means its mark went away. That makes 'searched and not found' a real possibility, so the comparison to רבי מאיר and the חכמים still works.
steps.whatToRemember: Two versions of רבי יוחנן. First (רבי חייא בר אבא): searched and not found, like רבי מאיר and the חכמים, possible because a temporary blemish could heal. Second (רבי אסי): searched and found, like רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on whether 'the one found is the one lost'.

phrases.english: Say it was a temporary blemish and it healed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי חייא בר אבא's version against רבי אסי's argument.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blemish was temporary and healed, so the animal is still there but can't be identified. 'Not found' is therefore possible.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי חייא בר אבא accept רבי אסי's version?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the earlier question. Now it asks why רבי חייא בר אבא did not explain the case the way רבי אסי did.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא, what is his reason for not explaining it like רבי אסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the mirror-image question. It already explained why רבי אסי rejected רבי חייא בר אבא's version, and now it wants to know why רבי חייא בר אבא rejected רבי אסי's version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Steps 18-21 the גמרא looked at the argument from רבי אסי's side. Now it looks at it from רבי חייא בר אבא's side. Each אמורא explained the case differently, so the גמרא wants to hear each one's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not say (explain it) like...

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya bar Abba,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי אַסִּי?
phrases.english: what is the reason he did not explain it like Rabbi Asi?
phrases.notes: רבי אסי's version: a blemished animal was later found, like the grave that was found in the field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror question to Step 18. Now the other אמורא's reasoning is examined.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רבי חייא בר אבא did not explain the case as 'it was found', the way רבי אסי did.

steps.title: A field often has graves, but checked sacrificial animals rarely get blemishes
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא says the field comparison does not fit. People bury in fields all the time, so a found grave could be a different one. But קדשים that were already checked and found whole do not normally develop a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: It makes sense with a field. People normally bury in a field, so just as this person was buried there, another person could have been buried there too. But with קדשים, once they were checked and found whole, is it normal for a blemish to fall on them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא explains why the 'found it' version would not create a real argument for קדשים. Once one blemished animal is found, everyone would agree it is the one that was lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the field case, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל can worry that the found grave is a new one, because burials in fields are common. With קדשים that were checked and were whole, new blemishes are unusual. So if one blemished animal turns up, even the תנא קמא would assume it is the lost one, and there would be no מחלוקת. That is why רבי חייא בר אבא needed a different explanation of the case.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (granted) with regard to...
its normal way; what usually happens

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי חייא בר אבא is ruling on the field case itself. He uses the field only as a contrast to show why קדשים are different.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
It makes sense with a field,
since people normally bury in it,
so just as this person was buried in it,
another person could have been buried there too.
phrases.notes: So the found grave may not be the lost one.

phrases.english: But sacrificial animals,
once we checked them and they were found whole,
is it normal for a blemish to suddenly appear on them?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question. The expected answer is no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The field comparison fails. Graves in a field are common, but new blemishes on checked קדשים are rare. So in the 'found it' case, everyone would agree the found animal is the lost one, and no argument would remain.

steps.title: רבי אסי's reply: animals gore each other, so blemishes are common
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי answers that animals in a flock butt and gore each other, so blemishes do happen often. That means the field comparison does fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי אסי)? Since they gore each other, blemishes are common among them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי אסי's response to רבי חייא בר אבא's argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא בר אבא claimed new blemishes are rare. רבי אסי disagrees: animals fight and gore each other, so new blemishes are common, just like new graves in a field. So a found blemished animal could be a new one, and the argument can still exist.

keyTerms.meaning: and the other one (what would he say?)

steps.whatToRemember: The two אמוראים argue about whether blemishes among קדשים are common. רבי אסי says yes, because animals gore each other, so the field case is a good comparison. רבי חייא בר אבא says no, so the field case does not fit.

phrases.english: And the other one (Rabbi Asi)?
Since they gore each other,
a blemish is common among them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אסי's counter to Step 23's claim that blemishes are rare.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Blemishes are common because animals gore each other, so the comparison to the field holds.

steps.title: Challenge from a ברייתא about wool plucked from an unblemished firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רבי אסי's earlier rule in the name of ריש לקיש. The ברייתא says: if someone plucks wool from a בכור תם, the wool is forbidden even if the animal later got a מום and was slaughtered. The גמרא starts to infer: the reason it is forbidden is that it was תם.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: One who plucks wool from an unblemished firstborn, even though it later developed a blemish and he slaughtered it, the wool is forbidden. The reason is that it was unblemished...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge (מיתיבי) using a ברייתא about wool from a בכור. It begins an inference from the word 'תם', and the rest of the attack continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי אסי said in the name of ריש לקיש that wool is forbidden unless an expert permitted the בכור before the wool fell off. The ברייתא forbids the wool specifically because the animal was תם (unblemished) when it was plucked. The גמרא is about to infer that if the animal was already blemished, the wool would be permitted even without an expert. That would contradict רבי אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (from a תנאי source, a משנה or ברייתא)
the reason is because... (signals an inference)

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not finished yet. 'טעמא דתם' only sets up the inference: the reason is that it was unblemished, which implies a blemished one would be permitted. The full contradiction is spelled out on the next amud.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who plucks wool from an unblemished firstborn,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנּוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם
phrases.english: even though a blemish later developed in it
and he slaughtered it, the wool is forbidden.
The reason is that it was unblemished,
phrases.notes: This begins the inference. The implied contrast (a blemished one would be permitted) continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the field and flock discussion and returns to רבי אסי's earlier ruling (in the name of ריש לקיש) about wool of a בכור.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's rule in the name of ריש לקיש: wool is forbidden if an expert did not permit the בכור before the wool was shed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids the wool because the animal was תם. This implies that wool from an already-blemished בכור would be permitted, even with no expert's permission. That contradicts רבי אסי.
